title: Separation of a gluing by valuatively saturated generic translates
statement:
Let $D$ be a discrete valuation ring, $F=\operatorname{Frac}D$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $B/S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and write $G=B_F$ [def-pc-base-change]. A commutative group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse morphisms satisfying the commutative group diagrams. Separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Locally of finite type and finite type have the meanings of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose that, for every local injective map $D\to V$ to a valuation ring with fraction field $L$, one has
$$\{a\in G(F):a_L\in B(V)\}=B(D).$$
Here a valuation ring is an integral domain $V$ such that for each nonzero $x\in L$ either $x$ or $x^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Put $\Gamma=G(F)/B(D)$ and choose representatives $a_\gamma\in G(F)$. For each $\gamma$ take a copy $B_\gamma$ of $B$. Glue distinct copies along their full generic fibres with transition $b\mapsto a_\eta^{-1}a_\gamma b$ from the generic fibre of $B_\gamma$ to that of $B_\eta$ [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes]. The resulting $S$-scheme $Z$ is smooth, separated and locally of finite type. Each chart is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], the generic-fibre identifications $b\mapsto a_\gamma b$ identify $Z_F$ with $G$, and two distinct charts have exactly $G$ as their intersection. This assertion does not assume that $B$ is a Néron model or an extension by a torus.

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$. The generic point of $S$ is open: a nonzero prime of the local principal ideal domain $D$ has a prime generator, which is irreducible; any proper principal ideal containing it has an associate generator, so that prime is maximal. Thus $(0)$ and $(\pi)$ are the only primes. The open complement of $(\pi)$, with its induced scheme structure, is $\operatorname{Spec}F$. Consequently $B_F$ is an open subscheme of $B$. Put $U_{\gamma\gamma}=B_\gamma$ and $U_{\gamma\eta}=(B_\gamma)_F$ for $\gamma\ne\eta$. Translation by $a_\eta^{-1}a_\gamma$ is an isomorphism with inverse translation by $a_\gamma^{-1}a_\eta$, by the group identities. The cocycle identity is $(a_\theta^{-1}a_\eta)(a_\eta^{-1}a_\gamma)b=a_\theta^{-1}a_\gamma b$. The overlap conditions also hold when indices coincide. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] to obtain $Z$ and covering open immersions $j_\gamma:B_\gamma\to Z$. The structure maps to $S$ glue to $Z\to S$: the continuous maps agree on overlaps, and for each open of $S$ the maps on sections glue by the sheaf axiom; on stalks the resulting map is one of the local chart maps, hence local. This also proves uniqueness of the glued morphism.

proof.text: On each generic chart define $q_\gamma(b)=a_\gamma b$. On its overlap with chart $\eta$, one has $q_\eta(a_\eta^{-1}a_\gamma b)=q_\gamma(b)$. The same sheaf gluing of morphisms as in step 1 gives $q:Z_F\to G$. Its inverse is the composite $G\xrightarrow{b\mapsto a_\gamma^{-1}b}(B_\gamma)_F\to Z_F$ for any fixed $\gamma$; the cocycle identity makes it independent of that choice. The group quotient $\Gamma$ contains the identity class, so a chart exists. Both inverse identities can be checked on the covering charts. The intersection statement of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] identifies distinct charts scheme-theoretically with this full generic fibre. The affine finite-type covers of the charts together cover $Z$, so $Z\to S$ is locally of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Since each chart map to $S$ is smooth, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] proves smoothness of $Z\to S$.

proof.text: Every ideal of $D$ is principal, hence finitely generated, so $D$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and its single affine chart makes $S$ locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. By [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], both $B$ and $Z$ are locally Noetherian: $B\to S$ is finite type by hypothesis and $Z\to S$ is locally of finite type by step 2. Thus [lem-sfb-locnoeth-valuative-separatedness] applies to both maps. In particular, because $B\to S$ is separated, any two $V$-points of $B$ over the same $S$-map which agree over $L=\operatorname{Frac}V$ are equal. Applying this with $V=D$ also justifies viewing $B(D)$ as a subgroup of $G(F)$.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), with Schemes Tags 01KZ and 01L0 for valuative uniqueness

proof.text: Let $V$ be any valuation ring, $L=\operatorname{Frac}V$, and let $u,v:\operatorname{Spec}V\to Z$ be over the same map $\operatorname{Spec}V\to S$ and agree over $L$. A valuation ring is local: if $x,y$ are nonunits, divisibility compares them, so $x+y$ is a multiple of a nonunit and is a nonunit; the nonunits form the unique maximal ideal. An open subset of its spectrum containing this closed point is the whole spectrum, since every prime lies in that maximal ideal. Choose charts containing the images of the closed point under $u$ and $v$; both maps therefore factor through entire charts, giving $x,y\in B(V)$ and indices $\gamma,\eta$. If $\gamma=\eta$, the injectivity of the chart map on morphisms and the uniqueness for $B$ from step 3 give $u=v$. If $\gamma\ne\eta$, equality on $\operatorname{Spec}L$ puts their common restriction in the intersection of the two charts, namely $G$. Therefore $D\to L$ is injective. Since $V\subset L$, the map $D\to V$ is injective too. This rules out every noninjective structural map without applying the saturation hypothesis.

proof.text: Continue with distinct chart indices and injective $D\to V$. If $\pi$ is a unit in $V$, the map factors through $F$: its prime kernels cannot be $(\pi)$, and every nonzero element of $D$ is invertible in $V$. Thus $x,y$ factor through the generic fibres of their charts. Put $c=a_\gamma^{-1}a_\eta\in G(F)$. It gives a $V$-point of $B_F\subset B$. The equality of generic restrictions in the coordinates of step 2 is $a_\gamma x_L=a_\eta y_L$, hence $x_L=c_Ly_L$. The two $V$-points $x$ and $cy$ of $B$ agree over $L$, so step 3 gives $x=cy$. This is precisely the gluing transition from chart $\eta$ to chart $\gamma$; hence their images $u,v$ in $Z$ are equal.

source.place: Tags 01JB (lemma-glue), 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes), 01KZ (lemma-separated-implies-valuative), 01L0 (lemma-valuative-criterion-separatedness); agent argument for saturated generic translates inspired by BLR 10.1 Example 5 and Proposition 7

proof.text: In the remaining case $\pi$ is not a unit in $V$. The contraction of the maximal ideal of $V$ is then $(\pi)$, so $D\to V$ is a local injective map and the stated saturation hypothesis applies. As before, $a_\gamma x_L=a_\eta y_L$, so the rational point $a_\eta^{-1}a_\gamma$ becomes $y_Lx_L^{-1}$, which is the restriction of the $V$-point $yx^{-1}\in B(V)$. Saturation gives $a_\eta^{-1}a_\gamma\in B(D)$. Their classes in $G(F)/B(D)$ are equal, contradicting $\gamma\ne\eta$. Thus this last case of distinct charts is impossible. Together steps 4–6 establish valuative uniqueness for every map $\operatorname{Spec}V\to S$, including the maps through the special point, the maps through the generic point, and field valuation rings. Applying [lem-sfb-locnoeth-valuative-separatedness] to the locally Noetherian $Z$ of step 3 proves that $Z\to S$ is separated. All the other asserted properties were established in steps 1–2.

Step 2: the map q:Z_F→G is well defined and its inverse does not depend on the chart, by the cocycle; locally of finite type follows from the definition, and smoothness from the Mathlib leaf on locality on the source. Step 3: by 01T6, B and Z are locally Noetherian; with V=D this also gives B(D)⊂G(F) and B(V)⊂G(L), which the saturation hypothesis needs. Step 4: a valuation ring is local, so u and v factor through charts; if γ≠η the common L-point lies in Z_F, so D→V is injective. Step 6 (π not a unit): D→V is local and injective, y_L x_L^{-1}=a_η^{-1}a_γ, and saturation puts this in B(D), contradicting γ≠η.
